evidence.evidence_text: LLM-as-a-judge has become a promising paradigm for using large language models (LLMs) to evaluate natural language generation (NLG), but the uncertainty of its evaluation remains underexplored.
This work presents the first framework to analyze the uncertainty by offering a prediction interval of LLM-based scoring via conformal prediction.
Conformal prediction constructs continuous prediction intervals from a single evaluation run, and we design an ordinal boundary adjustment for discrete rating tasks.
We also suggest a midpoint-based score within the interval as a low-bias alternative to raw model score and weighted average.
We also explore the usefulness of interval midpoint and judge reprompting for better judgment.
